system.summary: A numerical code of words, syllables and letters with values up to about 1,600 in no alphabetical order (Jefferson's Code No. 15); groups separated by dots, '=' after a group adds a plural s, '+' or 'x' marks -ed.
system.sibling_key: No key sheet is known; the PTJ editors say they could not reconstruct significant portions of Codes Nos. 14 and 15 (note to Pinckney, 20 Jun 1793). No key on origin/main shares its values (checked 27 Nov 2026).
system.notes: distinct_symbols = groups in key.tsv (206, from the 378 legible groups of the four documents). The 19 Mar 1793 postscript in this code survives only on the press copy (South Carolina Historical Society) and Morris's extract of 2 Mar 1793 only in NARA's unfilmed Duplicate Despatches; neither is here.

prior_solution.where: All four passages carry a decipherment of the time (Taylor's or Jefferson's interlinear) or, for 1 Jan 1793, a clear file copy; all are printed in PTJ 25 (1992) and on Founders Online. Upstream research/founders_emlo/founders_hits.tsv (lines 27-28) lists these letters as read from those decipherments. The key itself had not been rebuilt: the PTJ editors say they could not reconstruct significant portions of it.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling chose the lead and set the rules (a held-out passage chosen and a FreeTSA-stamped freeze before the single test run). AI agents fetched the images, transcribed, aligned, built and tested the key, and wrote this up. No person has read the groups or the alignment against the images. The images are NARA and Library of Congress public scans.
tools: NARA catalog media server and LoC image server (curl)

solution.what: Rotunda sweep (Andrew Beling's trial) found the PTJ editors' note that Codes Nos. 14 and 15 could not be reconstructed; checked origin/main for any target, key or claim (none).
NARA M30 roll 2 frames 0050-0100 and 0331-0433 sampled; LoC mtj1 017 0559-0560; Code No. 15 found at frames 0077-0078, 0083, 0086 and LoC 0559.
379 groups (378 legible) transcribed blind by two AI agents; 371 agree, about 11 differ (8 digits, 3 marks).

Protocol written (23:50 EST) naming the 1 Jan 1793 letter as held-out; key v1 (174 groups) aligned by hand from the 5, 10 and 27 Apr letters against Taylor's and Jefferson's interlinears; manifest of SHA-256 stamped by FreeTSA 28 Nov 04:53:47 GMT.

Held-out test run once (23:53:52 EST): of 72 groups, 37 had a key value and 33 matched the clear file copy (0.892), coverage 0.458; 1,000 shuffled keys: best 11, p <= 0.001. Pass bar (precision >= 0.80, p <= 0.01) met.

After the test: two alignment errors behind three of the four misses corrected; a cold check by a fresh AI agent; key v3 (206 groups: 92 sure, 15 probable, 97 unsure, 2 conflicting) from all four letters.

Second held-out text sought: Pinckney's duplicates and Morris's coded extract of 2 Mar 1793 are in NARA's Duplicate Despatches (College Park, 57 bound volumes, not filmed or digitized); the Gouverneur Morris Papers at LoC are not online; M34 has no Code No. 15 passage in our sweep.

outcome.method_basis: Every passage carries a decipherment of the time between the lines or (1 Jan 1793) a clear file copy, and all are printed in PTJ 25. The work transcribed the groups, rebuilt the code's values from those decipherments, and tested the rebuilt key on a held-out letter; no word shown here was first obtained with the rebuilt key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: the four reading files (texts/*_reading.txt): 270 cipher words, 0 holes; the five struck groups of 27 Apr are not text

texts.label: Jefferson to Thomas Pinckney, Philadelphia, 1 Jan 1793 (Code No. 15)
texts.summary: Jefferson tells Pinckney that the President wants early word of any British troops embarking for America, above all for Quebec: their numbers, destination and object. Pinckney had lost his copy of the code and could not read it.

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to Jefferson, London, 5 Apr 1793 (Code No. 15)
texts.summary: After a conversation with Lord Grenville, Pinckney expects Britain to stop neutral ships carrying grain, provisions, naval stores or contraband to French ports, to seize enemy property in neutral ships, and to treat blockaded ports strictly; one regiment is to sail from Ireland to the West Indies, and allied successes in the Netherlands may free more troops for that way.

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to Jefferson, London, 10 Apr 1793 (Code No. 15)
texts.summary: Britain's armament by sea and land continues with spirit; a division of France's dominions is talked of, with the French West Indies to go to Great Britain.

texts.label: Thomas Pinckney to Jefferson, London, 27 Apr 1793 (Code No. 15)
texts.summary: Negotiations are under way for a closer connection between Britain, Prussia and Austria; if the allies beat France their hatred of popular government may lead them to anything, so America should keep military stores such as nitre; few regular troops are left in Britain for distant expeditions.
